slides.title: First, Confirm the Board Series
slides.lead: Do not start with a command. Identify the series your board belongs to first.

cards.title: RDK X Series
cards.body: For products such as RDK X3, RDK X5, and RDK X5 Module.

cards.title: RDK S Series
cards.body: For products such as RDK S100, RDK S100P, and RDK S600.

cards.title: Check the Product
cards.body: Inside the manual, confirm that the selected product matches your device.

slides.title: Find the X5 Codec APIs
slides.lead: The goal is a repeatable search path, not memorizing a single interface.

steps.body: Open the RDK X3/X5 User Manual from GitHub IO.
Confirm that the current product is RDK X5.
Go to 3 Basic Application Development → 3.6 API Reference → RDK X5 → Python Interface.
Open Encoder Object or Decoder Object, then review API Reference.
Or search for Encoder, Decoder, encoding, or decoding in the upper-right corner.

slides.title: GitHub: Check Three Things
slides.lead: Use GitHub for official open-source projects, implementation details, and issue history.

cards.title: Right Repository
cards.body: Confirm that the repository name and purpose match your task.

cards.title: Right Branch
cards.body: Make sure the branch matches your board and platform.

cards.title: Read the README
cards.body: Review dependencies, directory structure, and usage before acting.

slides.title: Model Zoo: Pick the Board Branch
slides.lead: This lesson shows only the shortest lookup path. It does not download code or run a model.

steps.body: Choose rdk_x5; use rdk_x5_legacy only for historical examples.
Choose rdk_x3, then open the target task directory.
Choose rdk_s, then find the example by domain.
Read the target directory README before deciding the next step.
